sbc.text: The Company accounts for stock-based compensation in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification 718, Compensation – Stock Compensation , which requires that the estimated fair value on the date of grant be determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model with the fair value recognized over the requisite service period of the awards, which is generally the option vesting period. The Company’s determination of the fair value of the stock-based awards on the date of grant, using the Black-Scholes option pricing model, is affected by the fair value of the Company’s common stock as well as other assumptions regarding a number of highly complex and subjective variables. These variables include but are not limited to the Company’s expected stock price volatility over the term of the awards, and actual and projected employee option exercise behaviors. Because there is insufficient historical information available to estimate the expected term of the stock-based awards, the Company adopted the simplified method of estimating the expected term of options granted by taking the average of the vesting term and the contractual term of the option. The Company recognizes forfeitures as they occur when calculating stock-based compensation for its equity awards.

da.text: the year ended December 31, 2023, representing an increase of approximately $1.8 million, or 18%. This was driven by $1.6 million in higher third-party service costs due to outsourcing our field services, $1.2 million in higher scrap costs primarily related to our ASR hot-swap program, and $0.4 million in increased depreciation and amortization expenses; partially offset by a $0.8 million decrease in headcount expense, $0.4 million lower cellular and other software costs, and $0.2 million savings in rent, utilities and vehicle maintenance expenses compared to the same period in the prior year.

sbc.text: The Company accounts for stock-based compensation in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification 718, Compensation – Stock Compensation , which requires that the estimated fair value on the date of grant be determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model with the fair value recognized over the requisite service period of the awards, which is generally the option vesting period. The Company’s determination of the fair value of the stock-based awards on the date of grant, using the Black-Scholes option pricing model, is affected by the fair value of the Company’s common stock as well as other assumptions regarding a number of highly complex and subjective variables. These variables include but are not limited to the Company’s expected stock price volatility over the term of the awards, and actual and projected employee option exercise behaviors. Because there is insufficient historical information available to estimate the expected term of the stock-based awards, the Company adopted the simplified method of estimating the expected term of options granted by taking the average of the vesting term and the contractual term of the option. The Company recognizes forfeitures as they occur when calculating stock-based compensation for its equity awards.

In addition, the Company derives non-lease revenue items such as professional services related to ASRs’ deployments, special decals, shipping costs and training if any, recognized when control of these services is transferred to the clients, in an amount that reflects the consideration the Company expects to be entitled to in exchange for those services.

lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

The Company owns a trademark registration for its name “Knightscope” in the U.S. The Company relies and expects to continue to rely on a combination of confidentiality agreements with its employees, consultants, and third parties with whom it has relationships, as well as trademark, copyright, patent, trade secret, and domain name protection laws, to protect its proprietary rights.
Certain components used in our ECD products and other platforms are sourced from single suppliers or from a limited number of qualified suppliers.
During 2025, extended lead times from certain single-source or limited-source suppliers materially affected our ability to meet production schedules and customer delivery timelines.

Our ability to gain market share depends upon our ability to create demand, which includes increasing awareness about our products, satisfy client demands, enhance existing products and services and develop and introduce new products and services.

Our ability to gain market share also depends on a number of factors beyond our control, including the perceived value associated with our products and services, the public’s perception of the use of robots to perform tasks traditionally reserved for humans, and our clients’ acceptance of our view that security services can be performed more efficiently and cost-effectively through the use of our products and ancillary services.
As a result, you should not rely upon our past financial results as indicators of future performance.
Our ability to expand the market for our products depends on a number of factors, including the cost, performance and perceived value associated with our products and services.

We rely and expect to continue to rely on a combination of confidentiality agreements with our employees, consultants, and third parties with whom we have relationships, as well as trademark, copyright, patent, trade secret, and domain name protection laws, to protect its proprietary rights.
Our ability to gain market share depends upon our ability to satisfy client requirements, enhance existing products and develop and introduce new products.

The payment of any dividends on our Class A Common Stock will depend on earnings, financial condition and other business and economic factors affecting us at such time as our Board of Directors may consider relevant.

Investors may find our Class A Common Stock less attractive because we will rely on these exemptions, which could result in a less active trading market for our Class A Common Stock, increased price fluctuation, and a decrease in the trading price of our Class A Common Stock.

However, significant supply chain constraints, particularly affecting electronic components and certain single-source suppliers within our ECD product line, resulted in extended lead times, intermittent production interruptions, higher input costs, and delivery delays that impacted revenue timing and margin performance during the year.

Global electronic component shortages, tariff-related cost increases, and extended lead times from certain suppliers - some of which are single-source for specialized components - constrained production schedules and contributed to inconsistent shipment timing.

We derive our revenue from two primary sources: a) subscription MaaS offering which includes the ASRs as well as maintenance, service, support, data transfer, KSOC access, charging stations, and unlimited software, firmware and select hardware upgrades and b) the sale of ECD products and related recurring revenues from KEMS and full-service maintenance contracts.

The Company purchases inventory from an assortment of vendors worldwide; however certain components used in our ECD products and other platforms are sourced from single suppliers or from a limited number of qualified suppliers.
